## Description
Apache Commons BeanUtils introduced a feature to protect against access to the classloader through various mechanisms. The `declaredClass` property of Java enum objects is a vector for classloader access and not protected against by default. If an application passes property paths from an attacker directly to the `getProperty()` method of `PropertyUtilsBean`, the attacker can access the enumâs class loader via the `declaredClass` property. This can result in remote code execution (RCE).

fullDescription.text: Jenkins versions 2.56 and earlier as well as 2.46.1 LTS and earlier are vulnerable to an unauthenticated remote code execution. An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability allowed attackers to transfer a serialized Java `SignedObject` object to the Jenkins CLI, that would be deserialized using a new `ObjectInputStream`, bypassing the existing blacklist-based protection mechanism. We're fixing this issue by adding `SignedObject` to the blacklist. We're also backporting the new HTTP CLI protocol from Jenkins 2.54 to LTS 2.46.2, and deprecating the remoting-based (i.e. Java serialization) CLI protocol, disabling it by default.

Jenkins versions 2.56 and earlier as well as 2.46.1 LTS and earlier are vulnerable to an unauthenticated remote code execution. An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability allowed attackers to transfer a serialized Java `SignedObject` object to the Jenkins CLI, that would be deserialized using a new `ObjectInputStream`, bypassing the existing blacklist-based protection mechanism. We're fixing this issue by adding `SignedObject` to the blacklist. We're also backporting the new HTTP CLI protocol from Jenkins 2.54 to LTS 2.46.2, and deprecating the remoting-based (i.e. Java serialization) CLI protocol, disabling it by default.

fullDescription.text: In Eclipse Jetty, versions 9.2.x and older, 9.3.x (all configurations), and 9.4.x (non-default configuration with RFC2616 compliance enabled), transfer-encoding chunks are handled poorly. The chunk length parsing was vulnerable to an integer overflow. Thus a large chunk size could be interpreted as a smaller chunk size and content sent as chunk body could be interpreted as a pipelined request. If Jetty was deployed behind an intermediary that imposed some authorization and that intermediary allowed arbitrarily large chunks to be passed on unchanged, then this flaw could be used to bypass the authorization imposed by the intermediary as the fake pipelined request would not be interpreted by the intermediary as a request.

## Description
In Eclipse Jetty, versions 9.2.x and older, 9.3.x (all configurations), and 9.4.x (non-default configuration with RFC2616 compliance enabled), transfer-encoding chunks are handled poorly. The chunk length parsing was vulnerable to an integer overflow. Thus a large chunk size could be interpreted as a smaller chunk size and content sent as chunk body could be interpreted as a pipelined request. If Jetty was deployed behind an intermediary that imposed some authorization and that intermediary allowed arbitrarily large chunks to be passed on unchanged, then this flaw could be used to bypass the authorization imposed by the intermediary as the fake pipelined request would not be interpreted by the intermediary as a request.

## Description
Jetty is vulnerable to temporary directory Hijacking via a race condition. If code is executed from this temporary directory it can lead to local privilege escalation.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:orange_circle: [BDSA-2020-2949](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2020-2949)([CVE-2020-27216](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-27216)) - Race Condition due to Improper Synchronization


## Solution
Fixed in:
* [**11.0.0.beta3**](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-11.0.0.beta3)
* [**10.0.0.beta3**](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-10.0.0.beta3) 
* [**9.4.33.v20201020**](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-9.4.33.v20201020) by [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/53e0e0e9b25a6309bf24ee3b10984f4145701edb) commit and [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/9ad6beb80543b392c91653f6bfce233fc75b9d5f) commit.

## Workaround
Set a temporary directory, either for the server or the context, to one outside the shared temporary file system. For recent releases, a temporary directory by created by making a directory called work in the `${jetty.base}` directory (the parent directory of the webapps directory). Alternately the java temporary directory can be set with the System Property `java.io.tmpdir`. A more detailed description of how jetty selects a temporary directory is below.

To mitigate this vulnerability the directory must be set to one that is not writable by an attacker. To avoid information leakage, the directory should also not be readable by an attacker.

## Description
Eclipse Jetty does not correctly handle invalid HTTP/2 requests. An attacker could exploit this flaw to exhaust the HTTP/2 flow control window or TCP congest the connection. This will cause the relevant selector threads to be blocked and it will lead to a denial-of-service (DoS).

## Solution
Fixed in:
* **[9.4.47](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-9.4.47.v20220610)** by [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/be912d4315839405a8ae601f2e4ee0306867266e) commit,
* **[10.0.10](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-10.0.10)** and **[11.0.10](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-11.0.10)** by [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/b705091afb9158b39590fa36b9b84795524a8f0b) commit.

## Workaround
The vendor recommends users to filter the requests before they are sent to Jetty. One way to filter them would be to use a proxy.

## Description
Eclipse Jetty contains a vulnerability in its multipart request parsing mechanism that can lead to an out-of-memory error due to insufficient limiting measures. An attacker can exploit this flaw by supplying a request containing a large multipart without a filename in order to cause a denial-of-service (DoS).

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2023-0887](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2023-0887)([CVE-2023-26048](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-26048)) - Uncontrolled Resource Consumption


## Solution
Fixed in [**jetty-9.4.51.v20230217**](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-9.4.51.v20230217) by [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/c3021592218da289563987e6f7fbe05f8704b285) commit.

Fixed by [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/622befbd0d52f61c1acd41b4ef12458311494f1a) commit in:
* **[jetty-10.0.14](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-10.0.14)**
* **[jetty-11.0.14](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-11.0.14)**
* **[jetty-12.0.0.beta0](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-12.0.0.beta0)**

The latest stable releases can be found [here](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases).

## Workaround
It is recommended to set the multipart parameter `maxRequestSize` to a non-negative value in order to limit the whole multipart content. It has also been stated that limiting the multipart parameter `maxFileSize` will not be enough since the attacker can supply a large number of parts that, when summed up, will cause memory issues.

## Description
Apache Jackrabbit contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability in order to achieve remote code execution (RCE).

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:orange_circle: [BDSA-2023-1944](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2023-1944)([CVE-2023-37895](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-37895)) - Insecure Object Deserialization


## Solution
Fixed in [**2.21.18**](https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit/releases/tag/jackrabbit-2.21.18) by [this](https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit/commit/8a5df9df003240f0ffb045f6c8f86a8d6493129a) commit and [**2.20.11**](https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit/releases/tag/jackrabbit-2.20.11) by [this](https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit/commit/39173c683fb6a327c7a3a3bf7ed040168f27580f) commit.

The latest stable releases can be found [here](https://github.com/apache/jackrabbit/tags).

## Workaround
The vendor has provided the following workaround [here](https://lists.apache.org/thread/j03b3qdhborc2jrhdc4d765d3jkh8bfw):
> Turning off RMIFind web.xml (either in JAR/WAR file or in unpacked web application folder), and remove the declaration and the mapping definition for the RemoteBindingServlet:

        `<servlet>
            <servlet-name>RMI</servlet-name>
            <servlet-class>org.apache.jackrabbit.servlet.remote.RemoteBindingServlet</servlet-class>
        </servlet>

        <servlet-mapping>
            <servlet-name>RMI</servlet-name>
            <url-pattern>/rmi</url-pattern>
        </servlet-mapping>`

> Find the bootstrap.properties file (in `$REPOSITORY_HOME`), and set

         `rmi.enabled=false`

 >   and also remove

				`rmi.host
         rmi.port
         rmi.url-pattern`

> If there is no file named bootstrap.properties in `$REPOSITORY_HOME`, it is located somewhere in the classpath. In this case, place a copy in `$REPOSITORY_HOME` and modify it as explained.

## Description
Apache Ant is vulnerable to information disclosure due to the usage of a default temporary directory for several tasks. Some tasks may also allow the integrity of a build to be damaged.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2020-1128](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2020-1128)([CVE-2020-1945](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-1945)) - Sensitive Data Exposure


## Solution
Fixed in [**1.10.9-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.9_RC1) by [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/87ac51d3c22bcf7cfd0dc07cb0bd04a496e0d428) commit.

## Workaround
Steps were added to vulnerable versions to work around the issue. 

In [**1.9.15-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/rel%2F1.9.15) and [**1.10.8-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.8_RC1), the vendor has added [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/9c1f4d905da59bf446570ac28df5b68a37281f35) commit and [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/926f339ea30362bec8e53bf5924ce803938163b7) commit. 

The changes introduce the `ant.tmpdir` property which holds the safe directory path for temporary files. It has to be set by the user. The directory itself should also be set up by the user since Ant may not have the correct permissions to do it automatically.

In [**1.10.8-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.8_RC1), [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/a8645a151bc706259fb1789ef587d05482d98612) commit was also added. It attempts to set secure temporary file permissions, but does not protect the directory. 

Therefore it is strongly recommended that users set up a private secure temporary directory with appropriate permissions.

The official mitigation for versions from **1.1** to **1.9.14** and **1.10.0** to **1.10.7** is setting the `java.io.tmpdir` system property to point to a directory only readable and writable by the current user prior to running Ant.

Versions **1.9.15** and **1.10.8** can be trusted to use the Ant property `ant.tmpfile`, but the vendor still highly recommends using a safer private temporary directory instead.

## Solution
Fixed in [**ANT_1.10.9_RC1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.9_RC1) by [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/87ac51d3c22bcf7cfd0dc07cb0bd04a496e0d428) commit and [this](http://link-to-the-commit.com) commit.

## Workaround
**Note:** Per the vendor, The best mitigation still is to make Ant use a directory that is only readable and writable by the current user.

The official mitigation for versions from **1.1** to **1.9.14** and **1.10.0** to **1.10.7** is setting the `java.io.tmpdir` system property to point to a directory only readable and writable by the current user prior to running Ant.

Versions **1.9.15** and **1.10.8** can be trusted to use the Ant property `ant.tmpfile`, but the vendor still highly recommends using a safer private temporary directory instead.

Ant **1.10.9** will also try to create a temporary directory only accessible by the current user if neither of the properties above is set but may fail to create one if the underlying filesystem doesn't allow it.

Explicitly setting up a directory to use and set the respective property is the only mitigation that will work on every platform.

This issue affects Apache Commons Lang: Starting with commons-lang:commons-lang 2.0 to 2.6, and, from org.apache.commons:commons-lang3 3.0 before 3.18.0.

StackOverflowError could cause an application to stop.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.18.0, which fixes the issue.

fullDescription.text: In Eclipse Jetty, versions 9.2.x and older, 9.3.x (all configurations), and 9.4.x (non-default configuration with RFC2616 compliance enabled), transfer-encoding chunks are handled poorly. The chunk length parsing was vulnerable to an integer overflow. Thus a large chunk size could be interpreted as a smaller chunk size and content sent as chunk body could be interpreted as a pipelined request. If Jetty was deployed behind an intermediary that imposed some authorization and that intermediary allowed arbitrarily large chunks to be passed on unchanged, then this flaw could be used to bypass the authorization imposed by the intermediary as the fake pipelined request would not be interpreted by the intermediary as a request.

## Description
In Eclipse Jetty, versions 9.2.x and older, 9.3.x (all configurations), and 9.4.x (non-default configuration with RFC2616 compliance enabled), transfer-encoding chunks are handled poorly. The chunk length parsing was vulnerable to an integer overflow. Thus a large chunk size could be interpreted as a smaller chunk size and content sent as chunk body could be interpreted as a pipelined request. If Jetty was deployed behind an intermediary that imposed some authorization and that intermediary allowed arbitrarily large chunks to be passed on unchanged, then this flaw could be used to bypass the authorization imposed by the intermediary as the fake pipelined request would not be interpreted by the intermediary as a request.

## Description
Jetty is vulnerable to temporary directory Hijacking via a race condition. If code is executed from this temporary directory it can lead to local privilege escalation.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:orange_circle: [BDSA-2020-2949](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2020-2949)([CVE-2020-27216](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-27216)) - Race Condition due to Improper Synchronization


## Solution
Fixed in:
* [**11.0.0.beta3**](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-11.0.0.beta3)
* [**10.0.0.beta3**](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-10.0.0.beta3) 
* [**9.4.33.v20201020**](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-9.4.33.v20201020) by [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/53e0e0e9b25a6309bf24ee3b10984f4145701edb) commit and [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/9ad6beb80543b392c91653f6bfce233fc75b9d5f) commit.

## Workaround
Set a temporary directory, either for the server or the context, to one outside the shared temporary file system. For recent releases, a temporary directory by created by making a directory called work in the `${jetty.base}` directory (the parent directory of the webapps directory). Alternately the java temporary directory can be set with the System Property `java.io.tmpdir`. A more detailed description of how jetty selects a temporary directory is below.

To mitigate this vulnerability the directory must be set to one that is not writable by an attacker. To avoid information leakage, the directory should also not be readable by an attacker.

## Description
Eclipse Jetty contains a vulnerability in its multipart request parsing mechanism that can lead to an out-of-memory error due to insufficient limiting measures. An attacker can exploit this flaw by supplying a request containing a large multipart without a filename in order to cause a denial-of-service (DoS).

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)

## Solution
Fixed in [**jetty-9.4.51.v20230217**](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-9.4.51.v20230217) by [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/c3021592218da289563987e6f7fbe05f8704b285) commit.

Fixed by [this](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/commit/622befbd0d52f61c1acd41b4ef12458311494f1a) commit in:
* **[jetty-10.0.14](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-10.0.14)**
* **[jetty-11.0.14](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases/tag/jetty-11.0.14)**

The latest stable releases can be found [here](https://github.com/eclipse/jetty.project/releases).

## Workaround
It is recommended to set the multipart parameter `maxRequestSize` to a non-negative value in order to limit the whole multipart content. It has also been stated that limiting the multipart parameter `maxFileSize` will not be enough since the attacker can supply a large number of parts that, when summed up, will cause memory issues.

## Description
For Eclipse Jetty versions <= 9.4.40, <= 10.0.2, <= 11.0.2, if an exception is thrown from the SessionListener#sessionDestroyed() method, then the session ID is not invalidated in the session ID manager. On deployments with clustered sessions and multiple contexts this can result in a session not being invalidated. This can result in an application used on a shared computer being left logged in.

## Workaround
The author of the original advisory developed a temporary fix - due to an official solution not being available at the time of disclosure - which involves adding the following code to the `functions.php` file of the currently active theme/child-theme:

```
add_filter( 'wp_update_attachment_metadata', 'rips_unlink_tempfix' );

function rips_unlink_tempfix( $data ) {
    if( isset($data['thumb']) ) {
        $data['thumb'] = basename($data['thumb']);
    }

    return $data;
}
```

Please be aware that unless otherwise indicated, this third party workaround may not be fully tested and should be considered as a temporary measure only.

fullDescription.text:
WordPress is an open publishing platform for the Web. It's possible for a file of a type other than a zip file to be submitted as a new plugin by an administrative user on the Plugins -> Add New -> Upload Plugin screen in WordPress. If FTP credentials are requested for installation (in order to move the file into place outside of the `uploads` directory) then the uploaded file remains temporary available in the Media Library despite it not being allowed. If the `DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT` constant is set to `true` on the site _and_ FTP credentials are required when uploading a new theme or plugin, then this technically allows an remote code execution (RCE) when the user would otherwise have no means of executing arbitrary PHP code. This issue _only_ affects Administrator level users on single site installations, and Super Admin level users on Multisite installations where it's otherwise expected that the user does not have permission to upload or execute arbitrary PHP code. Lower level users are not affected. Sites where the `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS` constant is set to `true` are not affected. Sites where an administrative user either does not need to enter FTP credentials or they have access to the valid FTP credentials, are not affected. 


**Note: CVE details have been utilized in generating this advisory. The details of the vulnerability have not been independently verified by BlackDuck CyRC.**

## Description
Wordpress by default does not restrict access to certain directories which can be misused by unauthenticated users.

The lack of an Access Control List (ACL) allows anonymous and unauthenticated access to `wp-admin/load-scripts.php` which can be leveraged by an attacker to cause a denial of service condition by submitting an excessive list of script filenames via the `load` parameter.

## Description
WordPress is vulnerable to an object injection issue due to how the `upgrade_280()` function does not sufficiently validate values returned by the `get_results()` query.

## Description
WordPress is vulnerable to server side request forgery (SSRF) due to a possible time-of-check time-of-use attack . A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability in order to perform blind requests from the WordPress server to otherwise protected internal sites.

**NOTE:** An attacker would have to chain this behavior with another vulnerability to impact the targeted organization's security significantly.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2022-3598](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2022-3598)([CVE-2022-3590](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-3590)) - Server-Side Request Forgery




## Workaround
The following workaround is proposed [here](https://blog.sonarsource.com/wordpress-core-unauthenticated-blind-ssrf/):
> As a temporary workaround, we recommend system administrators remove the handler `pingback.ping` of the XMLRPC endpoint. One way to do this is to update functions.php of the theme in use to introduce the following call:
> ```
> add_filter('xmlrpc_methods', function($methods) {
>   unset($methods['pingback.ping']); 
>   return $methods; 
> });
> ```
> It is also possible to block access to xmlrpc.php at the web server level.

WordPress contains a file named `wp-cron.php` which is responsible for scheduled events. This file is triggered via HTTP request every time the site receives a visit, and works normally on sites with low visitor counts. However, with large enough amount of visits per minute, HTTP requests to ` wp-cron.php` may generate significant overhead by having to negotiate and establish the connection over a network socket. Unauthenticated attackers could abuse this behaviour to achieve denial-of-service (DoS).

fullDescription.text:
WordPress Core is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via user display names in the Avatar block in various versions up to 6.5.2 due to insufficient output escaping on the display name. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. In addition, it also makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that have the comment block present and display the comment author's avatar.

**Note: CVE details have been utilized in generating this advisory. The details of the vulnerability have not been independently verified by BlackDuck CyRC.**

## Description
WordPress is vulnerable to an information disclosure issue due to how `pingback.ping` XML-RPC requests can be abused. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted POST requests to the `XMLRPC` endpoint in order to enumerate the titles of private and drafted posts.

**Note:** The vendor does has stated that they will not fix this vulnerability.

## Workaround
The researchers who reported this vulnerability have suggested [here](https://www.imperva.com/blog/beware-a-threat-actor-could-steal-the-titles-of-your-private-and-draft-wordpress-posts/) that users can opt to use some form of WAF technology to protect against XML-RPC title leaks, or disable the `pingback` functionality completely on the WordPress site if it is not used.

## Description
A remote code execution (RCE) attack is possible when using the Struts REST plugin with `XStream` handler to deserialize XML requests.

This vulnerability is listed as exploitable by the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency in their [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:red_circle: [BDSA-2017-0903](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2017-0903)([CVE-2017-9805](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2017-9805)) - Insufficient XML Schema Validation


## Solution
Fixed in **[2.5.13](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_2_5_13)** by [this ](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/19494718865f2fb7da5ea363de3822f87fbda264)commit.
Fixed in **[2.3.34](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_2_3_34)** by [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/6dd6e5cfb) commit.

## Workaround
Various workarounds are possible as reported by the vendor:
1. Limit the Struts REST plugin to serve normal pages and JSONs only. Disable handling XML pages and requests to such pages.

`<constant name="struts.action.extension" value="xhtml,,json" />`

2. Override `getContentType` in `XStreamHandler`:

```public class MyXStreamHandler extends XStreamHandler { public String getContentType() {
 return "not-existing-content-type-@;/&%$#@";
 }
}```

3. Register the handler by overriding the one provided by the framework in your `struts.xml`:

`<bean type="org.apache.struts2.rest.handler.ContentTypeHandler" name="myXStreamHandler" class="com.company.MyXStreamHandler"/>`
`<constant name="struts.rest.handlerOverride.xml" value="myXStreamHandler"/>`

Fixed in versions:

## Workaround
An alternative solution is to switch to Jason Pell's multipart parser instead of the Commons-FileUpload library. The pell parser is a Struts 2 plugin, for more details see reference [url](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/S2PLUGINS/Pell+Multipart+Plugin).

It is possible to configure Apache's `mod_rewrite` to validate Content-Types and Tomcat requests using:

```
RewriteCond %{HTTP:Content-type} [$\#()%}{]
RewriteRule . [F,L]
RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} java.lang.ProcessBuilder
RewriteRule (.*) - [F]
```

## Description
Apache Struts is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE). This can occur when an attacker forces Struts to evaluate an Object Graph Navigation Library (OGNL) expression twice by supplying a crafted HTML request, resulting in malicious code being executed on the server within the context of the application. This is due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2016-0785 (BDSA-2016-1550).

## Solution
Fixed in:
* [**2.3.29**](https://archive.apache.org/dist/struts/2.3.29/)  with [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/b28b78c062f0bf3c79793a25aab8c9b6c12bce6e) commit.
* [**2.5.1**](https://archive.apache.org/dist/struts/2.5.1/) with [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/7da4ef39023bb5d86509d65565a04b533e8b4c55) commit.

The vendor states that some backward incompatibility issues can be expected when upgrading to Struts **2.3.29**. This is due to OGNL expressions that stop working because of performing disallowed arithmetic operations and assignments.

Please note that fixed versions of Apache Struts are hardened against malicious user input, however they will still allow forced double OGNL evaluation if the web application is designed to do so.

The vulnerability may allow a remote attacker to request data from internal resources that are not publicly available only by manipulating the processed input stream. Anyone relying on XStream's default blacklist can immediately switch to a whilelist for the allowed types to avoid the vulnerability. :orange_circle: [BDSA-2016-1550](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2016-1550)([CVE-2016-0785](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2016-0785)) - Weak Input Validation


## Solution
Partially fixed in:
* [**2.3.20.3**](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_2_3_20_3) by [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/717b2ec7d) commit.
* [**2.3.24.3**](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_2_3_24_3) by [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/036307bc0) commit.

The fix was improved in :
* [**2.3.29**](https://archive.apache.org/dist/struts/2.3.29/)  with [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/b28b78c062f0bf3c79793a25aab8c9b6c12bce6e) commit.
* [**2.5.1**](https://archive.apache.org/dist/struts/2.5.1/) with [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/7da4ef39023bb5d86509d65565a04b533e8b4c55) commit.

Please see BDSA-2016-1557 (CVE-2016-4461) for the improved fix.

Please note that fixed versions of Apache Struts are hardened against malicious user input, however they will still allow forced double OGNL evaluation if the web application is designed to do so.

The latest stable releases are available [here](https://struts.apache.org/download.cgi).

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2018-0878](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2018-0878)([CVE-2018-1327](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2018-1327)) - Insecure Object Deserialization


## Solution
Apache Struts version **[2.5.16](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_2_5_16)** implements the optional Jackson XML binding dependency by [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/pull/210/commits) commit.

To mitigate the denial-of-service vulnerability stemming from XStream library, switch to an optional Jackson XML handler or implement a custom XML handler based on the Jackson XML handler from the Apache Struts **2.5.16** as described [here](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/WW/REST+Plugin/#RESTPlugin-UseJacksonframeworkasJSONContentTypeHandler).

## Workaround
Use Jackson XML handler instead of the default XStream handler as described [here](http://struts.apache.org/plugins/rest/#custom-contenttypehandlers).

## Description
Apache Struts contains a denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability. An attacker is able to enter a null value for a URL field within the `URLValidator` class due to an overly permissive regular expression. This can lead to a crash.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2016-1554](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2016-1554)([CVE-2016-4465](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2016-4465)) - Uncontrolled Resource Consumption


## Solution
Partially fixed in version [**2.3.29**](https://archive.apache.org/dist/struts/2.3.29/) by [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/eccc31ebce5430f9e91b9684c63eaaf885e603f9) commit and version [**2.5.1**](https://archive.apache.org/dist/struts/2.5.1/) by [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/a0fdca138feec2c2e94eb75ca1f8b76678b4d152#diff-3b874b786a7e9059b3d4a2923c8b7d39) commit. Note that these are incomplete fixes.

The issue of the `URLValidator` regular expression blowup has been fixed in Apache Struts [**2.3.34**](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_2_3_34) and [**2.5.13**](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_2_5_13). See BDSA-2017-0922 for the fixing commits.

## Workaround
Instead of using the default `urlRegex` provided by the `UrlValidator` you can use the below one:

```
"^(?:https?|ftp):\\/\\/" +
"(?:(?:[a-z0-9$_.+!*'(),;?&=\\-]|%[0-9a-f]{2})+" +
"(?::(?:[a-z0-9$_.+!*'(),;?&=\\-]|%[0-9a-f]{2})+)?" +
"@)?#?" +
"(?:(?:(?:[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?\\.)*" +
"[a-z][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]" +
"|(?:(?:[1-9]?\\d|1\\d{2}|2[0-4]\\d|25[0-5])\\.){3}" +
"(?:[1-9]?\\d|1\\d{2}|2[0-4]\\d|25[0-5])" +
")(?::\\d+)?" +
")(?:(?:\\/(?:[a-z0-9$_.+!*'(),;:@&=\\-]|%[0-9a-f]{2})*)*" +
"(?:\\?(?:[a-z0-9$_.+!*'(),;:@&=\\-\\/:]|%[0-9a-f]{2})*)?)?" +
"(?:#(?:[a-z0-9$_.+!*'(),;:@&=\\-]|%[0-9a-f]{2})*)?" +
"$"
```

**Note**: This vulnerability was originally assigned **BDSA-2025-40342** (**CVE-2025-64775**), however it was assigned a new CVE as the original CVE did not mention several versions which were vulnerable.

## Description
Apache Struts is vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) due to a file leak during multipart request processing. This could allow a remote attacker to send crafted multipart requests. Successful exploitation could allow for disk exhaustion which could lead to a crash in the application.

**Note**: This vulnerability was originally assigned **BDSA-2025-40342** (**CVE-2025-64775**), however it was assigned a new CVE as the original CVE did not mention several versions which were vulnerable.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2025-54122](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2025-54122)([CVE-2025-66675](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-66675)) - Incomplete Cleanup


## Solution
Fixed in version [**6.8.0**](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_6_8_0) by [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/831568929cfba700f790f6ebe6e335f9f33fb468) commit and [**7.1.0**](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_7_1_0) by [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/824e7121b0796349f3ddfdf96bdc53936e0d37dd) and [this](https://github.com/apache/struts/commit/201b9e860e27627759d136d639157d701c959418) commit. 

However, the vendor recommends upgrading to version [**7.1.1**](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases/tag/STRUTS_7_1_1).

The latest stable releases can be found [here](https://github.com/apache/struts/releases).

## Workaround
The vendor has provided the following workaround [here](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/WW/S2-068):
Define a temporary folder used to store uploaded files with limited size or on the dedicated volume which won't affect system files. Or disable file upload support in the framework if not used.

## Description
Apache Struts contains an out-of-memory condition vulnerability due to insufficient validation of the sizes of non-file normal form fields in multipart requests. A privileged attacker could exploit this issue by passing a multipart request to a vulnerable instance which could trigger a denial-of-service (DoS) condition via excessive resource allocation.

## Description
Apache Struts2 contains a denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability.  This vulnerability requires an attacker to have the ability to upload a file to the server.  Under certain conditions, a remote attacker can then change the permissions of files and directories to read only.  This will prevent certain actions from working, causing errors.  This can be used to cause a denial-of-service.

The Struts 1 ActionForm object allowed access to the `class` parameter, which is directly mapped to the `getClass()` method. A remote attacker could use this flaw to manipulate the `ClassLoader` used by an application server running Struts 1. This could lead to remote code execution under certain conditions, allowing unauthorised disclosure of information, unauthorised modification and disruption of service.

Apache Commons BeanUtils is distributed in `lib/commons-beanutils-1.8.0.jar` in Apache Struts **1.x** to **1.3.10** and in other products requiring commons-beanutils (to version **1.9.2**)

## Description
Apache Ant is vulnerable to information disclosure due to the usage of a default temporary directory for several tasks. Some tasks may also allow the integrity of a build to be damaged.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2020-1128](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2020-1128)([CVE-2020-1945](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-1945)) - Sensitive Data Exposure


## Solution
Fixed in [**1.10.9-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.9_RC1) by [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/87ac51d3c22bcf7cfd0dc07cb0bd04a496e0d428) commit.

## Workaround
Steps were added to vulnerable versions to work around the issue. 

In [**1.9.15-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/rel%2F1.9.15) and [**1.10.8-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.8_RC1), the vendor has added [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/9c1f4d905da59bf446570ac28df5b68a37281f35) commit and [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/926f339ea30362bec8e53bf5924ce803938163b7) commit. 

The changes introduce the `ant.tmpdir` property which holds the safe directory path for temporary files. It has to be set by the user. The directory itself should also be set up by the user since Ant may not have the correct permissions to do it automatically.

In [**1.10.8-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.8_RC1), [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/a8645a151bc706259fb1789ef587d05482d98612) commit was also added. It attempts to set secure temporary file permissions, but does not protect the directory. 

Therefore it is strongly recommended that users set up a private secure temporary directory with appropriate permissions.

The official mitigation for versions from **1.1** to **1.9.14** and **1.10.0** to **1.10.7** is setting the `java.io.tmpdir` system property to point to a directory only readable and writable by the current user prior to running Ant.

Versions **1.9.15** and **1.10.8** can be trusted to use the Ant property `ant.tmpfile`, but the vendor still highly recommends using a safer private temporary directory instead.

## Solution
Fixed in [**ANT_1.10.9_RC1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.9_RC1) by [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/87ac51d3c22bcf7cfd0dc07cb0bd04a496e0d428) commit and [this](http://link-to-the-commit.com) commit.

## Workaround
**Note:** Per the vendor, The best mitigation still is to make Ant use a directory that is only readable and writable by the current user.

The official mitigation for versions from **1.1** to **1.9.14** and **1.10.0** to **1.10.7** is setting the `java.io.tmpdir` system property to point to a directory only readable and writable by the current user prior to running Ant.

Versions **1.9.15** and **1.10.8** can be trusted to use the Ant property `ant.tmpfile`, but the vendor still highly recommends using a safer private temporary directory instead.

Ant **1.10.9** will also try to create a temporary directory only accessible by the current user if neither of the properties above is set but may fail to create one if the underlying filesystem doesn't allow it.

Explicitly setting up a directory to use and set the respective property is the only mitigation that will work on every platform.

**Note** The attacker must be in control of the input to `response.redirect()` and the user must click before the redirect occurs.

## Description
Express.js contains an open redirect vulnerability due to insufficient validation of user supplied URLs. An attacker could exploit this by providing a crafted URL when performing a redirect bypassing the redirect allow list leading to an open redirect.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2024-0722](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2024-0722)([CVE-2024-29041](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-29041)) - Open URL Redirect


## Solution
Fixed in version [**4.19.0**](https://github.com/expressjs/express/releases/tag/4.19.0) and [**5.0.0-beta2**](https://github.com/expressjs/express/releases/tag/5.0.0-beta.2) by [this](https://github.com/expressjs/express/commit/0867302ddbde0e9463d0564fea5861feb708c2dd) commit.

Improved handling for the bypass was added in [**4.19.2**](https://github.com/expressjs/express/releases/tag/4.19.2) and [**5.0.0-beta.3**](https://github.com/expressjs/express/releases/tag/v5.0.0-beta.3) and  by [this](https://github.com/expressjs/express/commit/0b746953c4bd8e377123527db11f9cd866e39f94) commit.

The latest stable releases can be found [here](https://github.com/expressjs/express/tags).

## Workaround
The vendor has stated [here](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rv95-896h-c2vc) the following as a workaround  "The fix for this involves pre-parsing the url string with either `require('node:url').parse` or `new URL`. These are steps you can take on your own before passing the user input string to `res.location` or `res.redirect`."

## Description
XStream, when using some supported parsers, is vulnerable to an XML entity expansion issue due to how these parsers can process external entities by default.

A remote attacker could use this issue to retrieve the content of arbitrary files with known locations in a local file system if the Java process has read access.

**Note**: XStream is not vulnerable if the default XML Pull Parser (`Xpp3` or `kXML2`) is used. These parser types do not process XML entities.

## Solution
This vulnerability is fixed in version [**1.4.9**](http://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/com/thoughtworks/xstream/xstream/1.4.9/).

**Note**: Applications using one of the following parser implementations are still vulnerable:
* `DOM` implementation from Java 5 runtime and below
* `StAX` implementation from Java 6 runtime and below
* `StAX` implementation from BEA (old reference implementation)
* `XOM`

The latest stable releases are available [here](https://x-stream.github.io/download.html).

## Workaround
The vendor has recommended [here](https://x-stream.github.io/CVE-2016-3674.html) that users can opt to use one of the XML Pull Parser implementations in order to mitigate this issue.

## Solution
Fixed in [**1.4.19**](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/releases/tag/XSTREAM_1_4_19) by [this](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/commit/e8e88621ba1c85ac3b8620337dd672e0c0c3a846) commit.

The latest stable releases can be found [here](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/tags).

## Workaround
Per the Vendor [workaround](https://x-stream.github.io/CVE-2021-43859.html):

> If your object graph does not use referenced elements at all, you may simply set the NO_REFERENCE mode:
> ```
> XStream xstream = new XStream();
> xstream.setMode(XStream.NO_REFERENCES);
> ```
> If your object graph contains neither a Hashtable, HashMap nor a HashSet (or one of the linked variants of it) then you can use the security framework to deny the usage of these types:
> ```
> XStream xstream = new XStream();
> xstream.denyTypes(new Class[]{
> 	java.util.HashMap.class, java.util.HashSet.class, java.util.Hashtable.class, java.util.LinkedHashMap.class, java.util.LinkedHashSet.class
> });
> ```
> 
> Unfortunately these types are very common. If you only use HashMap or HashSet and your XML refers these only as default map or set, you may additionally change the default implementation of java.util.Map and java.util.Set at unmarshalling time:
> 
> ```
> xstream.addDefaultImplementation(java.util.TreeMap.class, java.util.Map.class);
> xstream.addDefaultImplementation(java.util.TreeSet.class, java.util.Set.class);
> ```
> However, this implies that your application does not care about the implementation of the map and all elements are comparable.

The vendor has stated [here](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/security/advisories/GHSA-j563-grx4-pjpv) that the following workaround can be implemented:

> The attack uses the hash code implementation for collections and maps to force recursive hash calculation causing a stack overflow. Following types of the Java runtime are affected:
>
> * java.util.HashMap
> * java.util.HashSet
> * java.util.Hashtable
> * java.util.LinkedHashMap
> * java.util.LinkedHashSet
> Other third party collection implementations that use their element's hash code may also be affected
> A simple solution is to catch the StackOverflowError in the client code calling XStream.
> 
> If your object graph does not use referenced elements at all, you may simply set the NO_REFERENCE mode:
> 
> XStream xstream = new XStream();
> xstream.setMode(XStream.NO_REFERENCES);
> If your object graph contains neither a Hashtable, HashMap nor a HashSet (or one of the linked variants of it) then you can use the security framework to deny the usage of these types:
> 
> XStream xstream = new XStream();
> xstream.denyTypes(new Class[]{
>  java.util.HashMap.class, java.util.HashSet.class, java.util.Hashtable.class, java.util.LinkedHashMap.class, java.util.LinkedHashSet.class
> });
> Unfortunately these types are very common. If you only use HashMap or HashSet and your XML refers these only as default map or set, you may additionally change the default implementation of java.util.Map and java.util.Set at unmarshalling time::
> 
> xstream.addDefaultImplementation(java.util.TreeMap.class, java.util.Map.class);
> xstream.addDefaultImplementation(java.util.TreeSet.class, java.util.Set.class);
> However, this implies that your application does not care about the implementation of the map and all elements are comparable.

The potentially dangerous types in this case are  `sun.awt.datatransfer.DataTransferer$IndexOrderComparator` and `java.io.FileInputStream`.

An attacker could supply a crafted input to XStream in order deletion arbitrary files on the local host.

## Description
Apache Ant is vulnerable to information disclosure due to the usage of a default temporary directory for several tasks. Some tasks may also allow the integrity of a build to be damaged.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2020-1128](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2020-1128)([CVE-2020-1945](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-1945)) - Sensitive Data Exposure


## Solution
Fixed in [**1.10.9-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.9_RC1) by [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/87ac51d3c22bcf7cfd0dc07cb0bd04a496e0d428) commit.

## Workaround
Steps were added to vulnerable versions to work around the issue. 

In [**1.9.15-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/rel%2F1.9.15) and [**1.10.8-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.8_RC1), the vendor has added [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/9c1f4d905da59bf446570ac28df5b68a37281f35) commit and [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/926f339ea30362bec8e53bf5924ce803938163b7) commit. 

The changes introduce the `ant.tmpdir` property which holds the safe directory path for temporary files. It has to be set by the user. The directory itself should also be set up by the user since Ant may not have the correct permissions to do it automatically.

In [**1.10.8-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.8_RC1), [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/a8645a151bc706259fb1789ef587d05482d98612) commit was also added. It attempts to set secure temporary file permissions, but does not protect the directory. 

Therefore it is strongly recommended that users set up a private secure temporary directory with appropriate permissions.

The official mitigation for versions from **1.1** to **1.9.14** and **1.10.0** to **1.10.7** is setting the `java.io.tmpdir` system property to point to a directory only readable and writable by the current user prior to running Ant.

Versions **1.9.15** and **1.10.8** can be trusted to use the Ant property `ant.tmpfile`, but the vendor still highly recommends using a safer private temporary directory instead.

## Description
Apache Ant is vulnerable to information disclosure due to the usage of a default temporary directory for several tasks. Some tasks may also allow the integrity of a build to be damaged.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2020-2577](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2020-2577)([CVE-2020-11979](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-11979)) - Sensitive Data Exposure


## Solution
Fixed in [**ANT_1.10.9_RC1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.9_RC1) by [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/87ac51d3c22bcf7cfd0dc07cb0bd04a496e0d428) commit and [this](http://link-to-the-commit.com) commit.

## Workaround
**Note:** Per the vendor, The best mitigation still is to make Ant use a directory that is only readable and writable by the current user.

The official mitigation for versions from **1.1** to **1.9.14** and **1.10.0** to **1.10.7** is setting the `java.io.tmpdir` system property to point to a directory only readable and writable by the current user prior to running Ant.

Versions **1.9.15** and **1.10.8** can be trusted to use the Ant property `ant.tmpfile`, but the vendor still highly recommends using a safer private temporary directory instead.

Ant **1.10.9** will also try to create a temporary directory only accessible by the current user if neither of the properties above is set but may fail to create one if the underlying filesystem doesn't allow it.

Explicitly setting up a directory to use and set the respective property is the only mitigation that will work on every platform.

## Description
The Ninja Forms Contact Form plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Self-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'Referer' header in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.15 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires "maintenance mode" for a targeted form to be enabled. However, there is no setting available to the attacker or even an administrator-level user to enable this mode. The mode is only enabled during a required update, which is a very short window of time. Additionally, because of the self-based nature of this vulnerability, attackers would have to rely on additional techniques to execute a supplied payload in the context of targeted user.

fullDescription.text:
Spring Framework is vulnerable to a flaw in the access restrictions to the security sensitive `ClassLoader` property. The restrictions can be bypassed through alternative paths available with Java9 and later. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to cause remote code execution (RCE).

**Note** this issue exists because the restrictions that were introduced to prevent exploitation of BDSA-2010-0001 (CVE-2010-1622) can be bypassed on platforms where Java9 and later are in use.

This vulnerability is listed as exploitable by the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency in their [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

fullDescription.text: Both Spring Security 3.2.x, 4.0.x, 4.1.0 and the Spring Framework 3.2.x, 4.0.x, 4.1.x, 4.2.x rely on URL pattern mappings for authorization and for mapping requests to controllers respectively. Differences in the strictness of the pattern matching mechanisms, for example with regards to space trimming in path segments, can lead Spring Security to not recognize certain paths as not protected that are in fact mapped to Spring MVC controllers that should be protected. The problem is compounded by the fact that the Spring Framework provides richer features with regards to pattern matching as well as by the fact that pattern matching in each Spring Security and the Spring Framework can easily be customized creating additional differences.

## Description
Spring Framework is vulnerable to a reflected file download (RFD) attack. An attacker can craft and send a URL with a `.bat` extension to a victim that results in the response being downloaded rather than rendered. Some input may also be reflected in the response.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:orange_circle: [BDSA-2015-0743](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2015-0743)([CVE-2015-5211](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2015-5211)) - Weak Input Validation


## Solution
Fixed in:
* [**3.2.15**](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/releases/tag/v3.2.15.RELEASE) by [this](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/commit/03f547) commit,
* [**4.1.8**](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/releases/tag/v4.1.8.RELEASE) by [this](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/commit/a95c3d) commit,
* [**4.2.2**](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/releases/tag/v4.2.2.RELEASE) by [this](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/commit/2bd1da) commit.

The latest stable releases are available [here](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/releases)

## Workaround
Upgrading to a fixed version will protect against RFD attacks. Additional protection can be implemented with the following steps:
* Set the content negotiation properties `useJaf` and `ignoreUknownPathExtension` to false. This will result in a `406` response for URLs with unknown extensions. This may not be an option if URLs are expected to have a dot towards the end.
* Spring Security 4 adds `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` header to responses by default. This may need to be done explicitly for earlier versions.
* An OWASP cross-site scripting (XSS) recommendation is that you encode JSON responses rather than escape them. An example of how to do this for Spring Framework can be seen [here](https://github.com/rwinch/spring-jackson-owasp). 
* Turn off or restrict suffix pattern matching to explicitly registered suffixes only.

Spring Framework, versions 5.0.x prior to 5.0.7 and 4.3.x prior to 4.3.18 and older unsupported versions, allows web applications to enable cross-domain requests via JSONP (JSON with Padding) through AbstractJsonpResponseBodyAdvice for REST controllers and MappingJackson2JsonView for browser requests. Spring MVC is vulnerable to XML external entity (XXE) injection as it does not disable external entity expansion by default and does not offer a way of disabling it manually. An attacker can leverage this flaw by sending crafted XML input to the server which may trick the XML parser into performing arbitrary operations on local resources that the attacker should not be able to control. This can lead to several problems ranging from an attacker being able to run stealth scans by bypassing the firewall, through sensitive information disclosure and denial-of-service (DoS), to server side request forgery (SSRF).

This CVE covers an incomplete fix to CVE-2013-7315.

NOTE: The fix to CVE-2013-6429 has also turned out to be incomplete (see BDSA-2014-0002 for details).

Spring Framework is vulnerable to server-side request forgery (SSRF) and an open redirect attack. An attacker could send a crafted HTTP request and deceive the application into making requests to unintended systems. This could enable an attacker to access confidential information or send harmful requests to other servers from the compromised system.

fullDescription.text:
Spring Security contains a flaw when dealing with OAuth2 access token empty scope list  responses. A remote attacker could leverage this to escalate their privileges under **all** the following conditions being met:

* They act as the role of a Login Client (e.g. uses `http.oauth2Login()`).
* They use one or more authorization rules with authorities mapped from authorized scopes (e.g. `anyRequest().hasAuthority("SCOPE_message.write")`) in the client application.
* An authorization server that responds with empty scopes list is registered (RFC 6749, Section 5.1).

**Note:** The role of Resource Servers (`http.oauth2ResourceServer()`) and applications that do not map authorization rules from authorized scopes (eg. `anyRequest().hasAuthority("ROLE_USER")`) cannot be exploited by this vulnerability.

fullDescription.text:
Spring Framework is vulnerable to a path traversal issue due to a lack of sufficient sanitization of path sequences processed by the `WebMvc.fn` or `WebFlux.fn` functional web frameworks.

A remote attacker could submit crafted HTTP requests to an application that serves static resources through the affected frameworks in order to read any file on the system that is accessible to the process in which the Spring application is running.

An application is vulnerable when both of the following are true:
* the web application uses `RouterFunctions` to serve static resources, and
* resource handling is explicitly configured with a `FileSystemResource` location

The vendor has noted in the official [advisory](https://spring.io/security/cve-2024-38819) that malicious requests are blocked and rejected when the Spring Security HTTP Firewall is in use.

**Note**: This issue exists due to an insufficient fix for the previously reported path traversal issue **CVE-2024-38816** (**BDSA-2024-6528**). Unlike **CVE-2024-38816**, applications deployed on Tomcat or Jetty are vulnerable.

fullDescription.text:
Spring Security is vulnerable to an information disclosure issue when `DaoAuthenticationProvider` is in use as a result of how timing attack defenses can potentially be bypassed.

Specifically, where an application is using the `UserDetails#isEnabled`, `#isAccountNonExpired` or `#isAccountNonLocked` user attributes, defenses can be bypassed for users who are disabled, expired or locked. Authentication can take different lengths of time to complete depending on user account state, which leaks some user attributes.

fullDescription.text:
The SSH protocol's specifications mandate insufficient integrity checks of Binary Packet Protocol (BPP) packets during a handshake. Message sequence numbers are not reset when encryption begins. A remote attacker in a network position between the client and server could leverage this to omit some negotiation messages, forcing a client and server to silently downgrade or disable some security features . This has been named a "Terrapin attack".

Practical attacks exist against multiple implementations of the protocol and encryption modes. The "chacha20-poly1305" SSH cipher has been shown to be exploitable. Ciphers using Encrypt-Then-MAC Message Authentication Codes (MACs) are theoretically exploitable under certain conditions.

## Description
Apache Commons FileUpload was discovered to be vulnerable to NULL byte poisoning due to the incorrect handling of filenames containing NULL bytes. ## Workaround
Applications utilising FileUpload prior to version **1.3.3** in the classpath can remediate by limiting the classes, including DiskFileUpload,  that are deserialized and through validation and verification of filenames in FileUpload control.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2023-0357](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2023-0357)([CVE-2023-24998](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-24998)) - Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling


## Solution
Fixed in Apache Commons FileUpload  version [**1.5-RC1**](https://github.com/apache/commons-fileupload/releases/tag/commons-fileupload-1.5-RC1) by [this](https://github.com/apache/commons-fileupload/commit/e20c04990f7420ca917e96a84cec58b13a1b3d17) commit.

The latest stable releases of Apache Commons FileUpload can be found [here](https://github.com/apache/commons-fileupload/tags).

However, it is stated that Apache Commons FileUpload does not enable any limits by default. Thus, after applying the fixing commit, the new configuration option `FileUploadBase#setFileCountMax` must be explicitly configured.

Fixed in Apache Tomcat:
* [**8.5.88**](https://github.com/apache/tomcat/releases/tag/8.5.88) by [this](https://github.com/apache/tomcat/commit/5badf94e79) commit,
* [**9.0.74**](https://github.com/apache/tomcat/releases/tag/9.0.74) by [this](https://github.com/apache/tomcat/commit/fbd8142162) commit,
* [**10.1.8**](https://github.com/apache/tomcat/releases/tag/10.1.8) by [this](https://github.com/apache/tomcat/commit/ba848da71c) commit,
* [**11.0.0-M5**](https://github.com/apache/tomcat/releases/tag/11.0.0-M5) by [this](https://github.com/apache/tomcat/commit/d53d8e7f77042cc32a3b98f589496a1ef5088e38) commit.

## Solution
Fixed in **[1.4.14](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/releases/tag/XSTREAM_1_4_14)** by [this](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/commit/0fec095d534126931c99fd38e9c6d41f5c685c1a) commit.

The latest stable releases are available [here](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/releases/).

## Workaround
The vendor has supplied the following workarounds if you rely on the blacklisting feature and are unable to upgrade to **1.4.14**.

For version **1.4.13**
Add two lines to XStream's setup code:
> 
> ```
> xstream.denyTypes(new String[]{ "javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter" });
> xstream.denyTypes(new Class[]{ java.lang.ProcessBuilder.class });
> ```
>
For versions **1.4.7** to **1.4.12** deny at least the following types: javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter, java.beans.EventHandler, java.lang.ProcessBuilder, java.lang.Void and void.
>```
> xstream.denyTypes(new String[]{ "javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter" });
> xstream.denyTypes(new Class[]{ java.lang.ProcessBuilder.class, java.beans.EventHandler.class, java.lang.ProcessBuilder.class, java.lang.Void.class, void.class });
> ```

For versions **1.4.6** or below, register a converter to prevent the unmarshalling of the currently know critical types of the Java runtime.
> ```
> xstream.registerConverter(new Converter() {
>   public boolean canConvert(Class type) {
>     return type != null && (type == java.beans.EventHandler.class || type == java.lang.ProcessBuilder.class || type == java.lang.Void.class || void.class || type.getName().equals("javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter") || Proxy.isProxy(type));
>   }
> 
>   public Object unmarshal(HierarchicalStreamReader reader, UnmarshallingContext context) {
>     throw new ConversionException("Unsupported type due to security reasons.");
>   }
> 
>   public void marshal(Object source, HierarchicalStreamWriter writer, MarshallingContext context) {
>     throw new ConversionException("Unsupported type due to security reasons.");
>   }
> }, XStream.PRIORITY_LOW);
> ```

## Description
XStream, when using some supported parsers, is vulnerable to an XML entity expansion issue due to how these parsers can process external entities by default.

A remote attacker could use this issue to retrieve the content of arbitrary files with known locations in a local file system if the Java process has read access.

**Note**: XStream is not vulnerable if the default XML Pull Parser (`Xpp3` or `kXML2`) is used. These parser types do not process XML entities.

* `StAX` implementation from Java 6 runtime and below

## Solution
Fixed in [**1.4.19**](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/releases/tag/XSTREAM_1_4_19) by [this](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/commit/e8e88621ba1c85ac3b8620337dd672e0c0c3a846) commit.

The latest stable releases can be found [here](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/tags).

## Workaround
Per the Vendor [workaround](https://x-stream.github.io/CVE-2021-43859.html):

> If your object graph does not use referenced elements at all, you may simply set the NO_REFERENCE mode:
> ```
> XStream xstream = new XStream();
> xstream.setMode(XStream.NO_REFERENCES);
> ```
> If your object graph contains neither a Hashtable, HashMap nor a HashSet (or one of the linked variants of it) then you can use the security framework to deny the usage of these types:
> ```
> XStream xstream = new XStream();
> xstream.denyTypes(new Class[]{
> 	java.util.HashMap.class, java.util.HashSet.class, java.util.Hashtable.class, java.util.LinkedHashMap.class, java.util.LinkedHashSet.class
> });
> ```
> 
> Unfortunately these types are very common. If you only use HashMap or HashSet and your XML refers these only as default map or set, you may additionally change the default implementation of java.util.Map and java.util.Set at unmarshalling time:
> 
> ```
> xstream.addDefaultImplementation(java.util.TreeMap.class, java.util.Map.class);
> xstream.addDefaultImplementation(java.util.TreeSet.class, java.util.Set.class);
> ```
> However, this implies that your application does not care about the implementation of the map and all elements are comparable.

## Description
XStream is vulnerable to denial-of-service due to a stack overflow that exists due to a recursive hash set calculation. A remote attacker could cause a vulnerable application to crash by causing that application to process a maliciously crafted input stream.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2022-3693](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2022-3693)([CVE-2022-41966](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-41966)) - Insecure Object Deserialization


## Solution
Fixed in version [**1.4.20**](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/releases/tag/XSTREAM_1_4_20) by [this](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/commit/e9151f221b4969fb15b1e946d5d61dcdd459a391) commit.

The latest stable releases can be found [here](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/tags).

## Workaround
The vendor has stated [here](https://github.com/x-stream/xstream/security/advisories/GHSA-j563-grx4-pjpv) that the following workaround can be implemented:

> The attack uses the hash code implementation for collections and maps to force recursive hash calculation causing a stack overflow. Following types of the Java runtime are affected:
>
> * java.util.HashMap
> * java.util.HashSet
> * java.util.Hashtable
> * java.util.LinkedHashMap
> * java.util.LinkedHashSet
> Other third party collection implementations that use their element's hash code may also be affected
> A simple solution is to catch the StackOverflowError in the client code calling XStream.
> 
> If your object graph does not use referenced elements at all, you may simply set the NO_REFERENCE mode:
> 
> XStream xstream = new XStream();
> xstream.setMode(XStream.NO_REFERENCES);
> If your object graph contains neither a Hashtable, HashMap nor a HashSet (or one of the linked variants of it) then you can use the security framework to deny the usage of these types:
> 
> XStream xstream = new XStream();
> xstream.denyTypes(new Class[]{
>  java.util.HashMap.class, java.util.HashSet.class, java.util.Hashtable.class, java.util.LinkedHashMap.class, java.util.LinkedHashSet.class
> });
> Unfortunately these types are very common. If you only use HashMap or HashSet and your XML refers these only as default map or set, you may additionally change the default implementation of java.util.Map and java.util.Set at unmarshalling time::
> 
> xstream.addDefaultImplementation(java.util.TreeMap.class, java.util.Map.class);
> xstream.addDefaultImplementation(java.util.TreeSet.class, java.util.Set.class);
> However, this implies that your application does not care about the implementation of the map and all elements are comparable.

XStream, when in its default configuration or operating without a sufficient blacklist / whitelist configuration, is vulnerable to an arbitrary file deletion issue. This is due to how XStream can potentially create new instances of dangerous objects that are not blocked based on the contents of the input stream. This is due to how XStream can potentially create new instances of dangerous objects that are not blocked based on the contents of the input stream. The potentially dangerous types in this case are  `sun.awt.datatransfer.DataTransferer$IndexOrderComparator` and `java.io.FileInputStream`.

An attacker could supply a crafted input to XStream in order deletion arbitrary files on the local host.

## Description
It was discovered that Bouncy Castle for Java was susceptible to excessive allocation issues due to a lack of restrictions on creation of ASN.1 OIDs from encodings. An attacker could exploit this by supplying crafted content in order to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) condition. 

**Note:** This issue does not apply to applications which do not consume unvetted, or otherwise unvalidated, ASN.1 encodings.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2025-8507](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2025-8507)([CVE-2025-8885](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-8885)) - Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling


## Solution
Fixed in Bouncy Castle Java [**r1rv78v1**](https://github.com/bcgit/bc-java/releases/tag/r1rv78v1) by [this](https://github.com/bcgit/bc-java/commit/3790993df5d28f661a64439a8664343437ed3865) commit.

The latest stable BC Java releases can be found [here](https://www.bouncycastle.org/download/bouncy-castle-java/).

Fixed in Bouncy Castle Java FIPS [**2.0.1**](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/org.bouncycastle/bc-fips/2.0.1) and [**1.0.2.6**](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/org.bouncycastle/bc-fips/1.0.2.6).

The latest stable BC Java FIPS releases can be found [here](https://www.bouncycastle.org/download/bouncy-castle-java-fips/).

## Workaround
The Vendor has suggested the following:
> Issue can be mitigated by placing a cap on the size of ASN.1 encodings that can be consumed from external sources in the "the wild", or by introducing some form of validation for such objects.

fullDescription.text: The default BKS keystore use an HMAC that is only 16 bits long, which can allow an attacker to compromise the integrity of a BKS keystore. Bouncy Castle release 1.47 changes the BKS format to a format which uses a 160 bit HMAC instead. This applies to any BKS keystore generated prior to BC 1.47. For situations where people need to create the files for legacy reasons a specific keystore type "BKS-V1" was introduced in 1.49. It should be noted that the use of "BKS-V1" is discouraged by the library authors and should only be used where it is otherwise safe to do so, as in where the use of a 16 bit checksum for the file integrity check is not going to cause a security issue in itself.

## Description
Apache Ant is vulnerable to information disclosure due to the usage of a default temporary directory for several tasks. Some tasks may also allow the integrity of a build to be damaged.

## Vulnerabilities(BDSA,CVE)
:yellow_circle: [BDSA-2020-1128](https://openhub.net/vulnerabilities/bdsa/BDSA-2020-1128)([CVE-2020-1945](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-1945)) - Sensitive Data Exposure


## Solution
Fixed in [**1.10.9-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.9_RC1) by [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/87ac51d3c22bcf7cfd0dc07cb0bd04a496e0d428) commit.

## Workaround
Steps were added to vulnerable versions to work around the issue. 

In [**1.9.15-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/rel%2F1.9.15) and [**1.10.8-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.8_RC1), the vendor has added [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/9c1f4d905da59bf446570ac28df5b68a37281f35) commit and [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/926f339ea30362bec8e53bf5924ce803938163b7) commit. 

The changes introduce the `ant.tmpdir` property which holds the safe directory path for temporary files. It has to be set by the user. The directory itself should also be set up by the user since Ant may not have the correct permissions to do it automatically.

In [**1.10.8-rc1**](https://github.com/apache/ant/releases/tag/ANT_1.10.8_RC1), [this](https://github.com/apache/ant/commit/a8645a151bc706259fb1789ef587d05482d98612) commit was also added. It attempts to set secure temporary file permissions, but does not protect the directory. 

Therefore it is strongly recommended that users set up a private secure temporary directory with appropriate permissions.

The official mitigation for versions from **1.1** to **1.9.14** and **1.10.0** to **1.10.7** is setting the `java.io.tmpdir` system property to point to a directory only readable and writable by the current user prior to running Ant.

Versions **1.9.15** and **1.10.8** can be trusted to use the Ant property `ant.tmpfile`, but the vendor still highly recommends using a safer private temporary directory instead.

**Note:** Per the vendor, The best mitigation still is to make Ant use a directory that is only readable and writable by the current user.

The official mitigation for versions from **1.1** to **1.9.14** and **1.10.0** to **1.10.7** is setting the `java.io.tmpdir` system property to point to a directory only readable and writable by the current user prior to running Ant.
