message.text: Apache Commons HttpClient is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks. The component fails to validate a server's hostname against a SSL certificate correctly. This could allow an attacker with a valid certificate to spoof as a trusted host.

Apache Commons HttpClient is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks. The component fails to validate a server's hostname against a SSL certificate correctly. This could allow an attacker with a valid certificate to spoof as a trusted host.

Apache HTTPClient is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks due to a flaw in the default hostname verification process. An attacker could leverage this flaw to spoof a valid certificate by supplying a specially crafted subject. The MITM position can then be used to sniff and modify passing traffic.

Apache HttpClient is vulnerable to the disclosure and modification of data due to the mishandling of malformed URIs. An attacker could pass a maliciously crafted request to a vulnerable application, which will then be executed on an incorrect host.

http/conn/ssl/SSLConnectionSocketFactory.java in Apache HttpComponents HttpClient before 4.3.6 ignores the http.socket.timeout configuration setting during an SSL handshake, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (HTTPS call hang) via unspecified vectors.

A series of deserialization vulnerabilities have been discovered in Codehaus 1.9.x implemented in EAP 7. This CVE fixes CVE-2017-17485, CVE-2017-7525, CVE-2017-15095, CVE-2018-5968, CVE-2018-7489, CVE-2018-1000873, CVE-2019-12086 reported for FasterXML jackson-databind by implementing a whitelist approach that will mitigate these vulnerabilities and future ones alike.

It was discovered that jackson-mapper-asl  is vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) attacks due to the unsafe implementation of parsing functionality. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability via a crafted request to execute an XML external entities (XXE) attack against the application.
Apache Jackrabbit contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability in order to achieve remote code execution (RCE).

Apache Jackrabbit is vulnerable to deserialization of untrusted data due to accepting JNDI URIs for JCR lookup from untrusted users. This could allow an attacker to inject malicious JNDI references, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution.

Apache Struts 2.0.0 through 2.3.24.1 does not properly cache method references when used with OGNL before 3.0.12, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (block access to a web site) via unspecified vectors.

Apache Maven is vulnerable to a repository hijacking style attack.  This is due to how Maven implements following links for dependencies in `pom.xml` files.  A remote attacker that is able to control a dependencies source repository or is able to man-in-the-middle the connection may be able to cause Maven to install malicious software.

The hoek module for Node is vulnerable to prototype pollution. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to modify the `Object` prototype which causes additional properties or changes to exist on all objects.

Node.js module Hoek is vulnerable to prototype pollution attack due to insufficient validation of user input. Local attackers could leverage this vulnerability to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
Node.js module sshpk is vulnerable to regular expression denial-of-service (ReDoS) due to a mistake in the implementation of regular expression matching.

Apache ant is vulnerable to an arbitrary file write vulnerability via a directory traversal. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying the component with a maliciously crafted archive that, when unpacked, would cause an arbitrary file to be written to the file system.
Apache Ant is vulnerable to information disclosure due to the usage of a default temporary directory for several tasks. Some tasks may also allow the integrity of a build to be damaged.
Apache Ant is vulnerable to information disclosure due to the usage of a default temporary directory for several tasks. Some tasks may also allow the integrity of a build to be damaged.

Apache Ant is vulnerable to an out of memory error via a crafted `TAR` archive. An attacker could exploit this in order to cause as denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

**Note:** Per the Vendor, "Versions prior to 1.9.0 are not affected when reading tar archives.".
Apache Ant is vulnerable to an out of memory error via a crafted `ZIP` archive. An attacker could exploit this in order to cause as denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
It was found that jenkins-ssh-slaves-plugin before version 1.15 did not perform host key verification, thereby enabling Man-in-the-Middle attacks.

Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in the Mailer Plugin 1.20 for Jenkins 2.111 allows remote authenticated users to send unauthorized mail as an arbitrary user via a /descriptorByName/hudson.tasks.Mailer/sendTestMail request.
Jenkins Mailer Plugin 1.32 and earlier does not perform hostname validation when connecting to the configured SMTP server.

A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in Jenkins Mailer Plugin 391.ve4a_38c1b_cf4b_ and earlier allows attackers to use the DNS used by the Jenkins instance to resolve an attacker-specified hostname.

A missing permission check in Jenkins Mailer Plugin 391.ve4a_38c1b_cf4b_ and earlier allows attackers with Overall/Read access to use the DNS used by the Jenkins instance to resolve an attacker-specified hostname.

jenkins-mailer-plugin before version 1.20 is vulnerable to an information disclosure while using the feature to send emails to a dynamically created list of users based on the changelogs. This could in some cases result in emails being sent to people who have no user account in Jenkins, and in rare cases even people who were not involved in whatever project was being built, due to some mapping based on the local-part of email addresses.

Spring Security is vulnerable to authentication bypass. A flaw in the handling of path parameters by servlet containers could allow an attacker to bypass the security constraints of a path parameter. If successful, the attacker could access restricted areas of the application without requiring credentials.

Uncontrolled Recursion vulnerability in Apache Commons Lang.

This issue affects Apache Commons Lang: Starting with commons-lang:commons-lang 2.0 to 2.6, and, from org.apache.commons:commons-lang3 3.0 before 3.18.0.

The methods ClassUtils.getClass(...) can throw StackOverflowError on very long inputs. Because an Error is usually not handled by applications and libraries, a 
StackOverflowError could cause an application to stop.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.18.0, which fixes the issue.
json-schema is vulnerable to prototype pollution attacks. This allows an attacker that is able to supply untrusted input to applications using json-schema to potentially execute malicious code.

In Eclipse Jetty, versions 9.2.x and older, 9.3.x (all configurations), and 9.4.x (non-default configuration with RFC2616 compliance enabled), transfer-encoding chunks are handled poorly. The chunk length parsing was vulnerable to an integer overflow. Thus a large chunk size could be interpreted as a smaller chunk size and content sent as chunk body could be interpreted as a pipelined request. If Jetty was deployed behind an intermediary that imposed some authorization and that intermediary allowed arbitrarily large chunks to be passed on unchanged, then this flaw could be used to bypass the authorization imposed by the intermediary as the fake pipelined request would not be interpreted by the intermediary as a request.

A remote attacker can send a specially crafted request with a malicious HTTP header that may be interpreted differently by an intermediate caching proxy.  This could allow an attacker to change the content provided by Eclipse Jetty for a specific URL.
A remote attacker can supply specially crafted content-length headers to Eclipse Jetty that may bypass the authorization checks of an intermediary caching proxy.

A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability has been detected in Jetty when open directory listing is enabled. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to send malicious links to target victim to execute code on their browser.

A cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability has been discovered in Eclipse Jetty. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by distributing a crafted link which can execute arbitrary code in the context of the victim's browser.
The HTTP/2 protocol allows a denial of service (server resource consumption) because request cancellation can reset many streams quickly, as exploited in the wild in August through October 2023.
Jetty is vulnerable to temporary directory Hijacking via a race condition. If code is executed from this temporary directory it can lead to local privilege escalation.

Jetty is vulnerable to information disclosure due to improper requested path verification. This allows crafted requests to access protected resources of the web application which, depending on the implementation, might reveal sensitive information.

A covert time channel vulnerability has been discovered in Jetty. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by observing system behavior between valid and invalid response times to obtain additional information, such as valid accounts names or passwords.

Eclipse Jetty does not correctly handle invalid HTTP/2 requests. An attacker could exploit this flaw to exhaust the HTTP/2 flow control window or TCP congest the connection. This will cause the relevant selector threads to be blocked and it will lead to a denial-of-service (DoS).

Eclipse Jetty contains a vulnerability in its multipart request parsing mechanism that can lead to an out-of-memory error due to insufficient limiting measures. An attacker can exploit this flaw by supplying a request containing a large multipart without a filename in order to cause a denial-of-service (DoS).

Eclipse Jetty does not properly parse quoted values in cookies. This could allow an attacker to smuggle cookies within other cookies into the application. The attacker can also tamper with the cookie parsing mechanism and cause other unintended behavior.

Eclipse Jetty is vulnerable to Denial-of-Service (DoS) via invalid TLS frames. An attacker could exploit this by sending a TLS frame with a size in excess of 17408 resulting in excessive resource consumption leading to a DoS condition.

An information exposure vulnerability has been discovered in Eclipse Jetty. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by navigating through the leaked base resource configurations to retrieve sensitive data from hidden directories.

Eclipse Jetty does not correctly handle invalid authority segments of HTTP URIs. An authenticated attacker could exploit this flaw by passing an invalid URI that contains an improper authority with no host so that it is interpreted as one with a host.

An insufficient validation issue has been identified in Eclipse Jetty.  A remote unauthenticated attacker could exploit this in order to carry out server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks or URL redirection via the `HttpURI` utility class. 

**Note:** The impact of this vulnerability is limited to developers that use the Jetty `HttpURI` directly.

For Eclipse Jetty versions <= 9.4.40, <= 10.0.2, <= 11.0.2, if an exception is thrown from the SessionListener#sessionDestroyed() method, then the session ID is not invalidated in the session ID manager. On deployments with clustered sessions and multiple contexts this can result in a session not being invalidated. This can result in an application used on a shared computer being left logged in.
WordPress is prone to SQL injection in `$wpdb->prepare()` database abstraction method via plugins provided arguments.
WordPress before 5.2.4 has a Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability because Windows paths are mishandled during certain validation of relative URLs.

SQL injection vulnerability in wp-includes/class-wp-query.php in WP_Query in WordPress before 4.7.2 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands by leveraging the presence of an affected plugin or theme that mishandles a crafted post type name.

The isMail transport in PHPMailer before 5.2.20 might allow remote attackers to pass extra parameters to the mail command and consequently execute arbitrary code by leveraging improper interaction between the escapeshellarg function and internal escaping performed in the mail function in PHP. NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incorrect fix for CVE-2016-10033.

The mailSend function in the isMail transport in PHPMailer before 5.2.18 might allow remote attackers to pass extra parameters to the mail command and consequently execute arbitrary code via a \" (backslash double quote) in a crafted Sender property.

WordPress is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) due to a remote file upload vulnerability.  This allows a remote attacker with the privileges as "author" to upload malicious file types that can then be used to execute code on the hosting server.

Note:  This RCE vulnerability works in conjunction with CVE-2019-8943 and CVE-2019-6977.

WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input allowing path traversal. This could allow an attacker to elevate their privileges by reinstalling a WordPress instance with administrator credentials of their choice.

PHPMailer 6.1.8 through 6.4.0 allows object injection through Phar Deserialization via addAttachment with a UNC pathname. NOTE: this is similar to CVE-2018-19296, but arose because 6.1.8 fixed a functionality problem in which UNC pathnames were always considered unreadable by PHPMailer, even in safe contexts. As an unintended side effect, this fix eliminated the code that blocked addAttachment exploitation.

Due to a [previous fix](https://wordpress.org/news/2017/09/wordpress-4-8-2-security-and-maintenance-release/) released in WordPress version **4.8.2** being insufficient,  the WordPress Core is vulnerable to SQL Injection (*SQLi*).  

Note: The WordPress core is not directly vulnerable.  The vulnerability arises when WordPress plugins or themes pass input into the `prepare()` function.

WordPress is prone to a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability.

WordPress contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This allows an attacker to inject malicious JavaScript into dynamically generated web content which will be executed in a victim's browser.
WordPess contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This allows an attacker to inject and execute JavaScript in a victim's browser.

NOTE: the approach to changing this may not be fully compatible with certain use cases, such as migration of a WordPress site from a web host that uses a recent PHP version to a different web host that uses PHP 5.2. These use cases are plausible (but very unlikely) based on statistics showing widespread deployment of WordPress with obsolete PHP versions.

An issue with values being overwritten in The `request_filesystem_credentials()` method can lead to Cross Site Request Forgery.
WordPress is vulnerable to insecure deserialization. In the worst case scenario this could potentially be exploited to inject PHP objects and achieve remote code execution (RCE).
WordPress is vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (*CSRF*) via widget editing functionality.
WordPress is vulnerable to access restriction bypass via Multisite WordPress API due to weak cryptographic security.

WordPress is vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting (XSS) due to improper validation of user-supplied input. This could allow an attacker to inject arbitrary web scripts and steal a user's session cookies.

WordPress is an open publishing platform for the Web. It's possible for a file of a type other than a zip file to be submitted as a new plugin by an administrative user on the Plugins -> Add New -> Upload Plugin screen in WordPress. If FTP credentials are requested for installation (in order to move the file into place outside of the `uploads` directory) then the uploaded file remains temporary available in the Media Library despite it not being allowed. If the `DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT` constant is set to `true` on the site _and_ FTP credentials are required when uploading a new theme or plugin, then this technically allows an remote code execution (RCE) when the user would otherwise have no means of executing arbitrary PHP code. This issue _only_ affects Administrator level users on single site installations, and Super Admin level users on Multisite installations where it's otherwise expected that the user does not have permission to upload or execute arbitrary PHP code. Lower level users are not affected. Sites where the `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS` constant is set to `true` are not affected. Sites where an administrative user either does not need to enter FTP credentials or they have access to the valid FTP credentials, are not affected. 


**Note: CVE details have been utilized in generating this advisory. The details of the vulnerability have not been independently verified by BlackDuck CyRC.**

WordPress is prone to Cross-Site Scripting (*XSS*) vulnerability via template names.
Wordpress is vulnerable to open redirects due to improper referrer URL validation. An attacker could send a crafted link that would redirect legitimate users to a malicious website.

Wordpress discloses the sender's email address in Post by Email logs in `wp-mail.php`. A remote unauthenticated attacker may obtain the email address of the user who posted a blog using the WordPress Post by Email Feature.
WordPress is prone to Cross-Site Scripting (*XSS*) vulnerability via the plugin editor.

Wordpress is vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF) in the `wp-trackback.php` page. An attacker could craft a link that points to that page, and send it to a logged in user. Once clicked, the page would then execute actions embedded in the link on the behalf of the user.
WordPress is prone to Cross-Site Scripting (*XSS*) vulnerability via visual editor.
WordPress is prone to Cross-Site Scripting (*XSS*) attack in `oEmbed` discovery.
WordPress is vulnerable to cross-site scripting attacks due to an insufficient check if a user has a valid customization session token.
WordPress is vulnerable to Unauthorised modification of content due to improper handling of post meta data values in the XML-RPC API.

WordPress is vulnerable to server side request forgery (SSRF) due to a possible time-of-check time-of-use attack . A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability in order to perform blind requests from the WordPress server to otherwise protected internal sites.

**NOTE:** An attacker would have to chain this behavior with another vulnerability to impact the targeted organization's security significantly.

WordPress contains a file named `wp-cron.php` which is responsible for scheduled events. This file is triggered via HTTP request every time the site receives a visit, and works normally on sites with low visitor counts. However, with large enough amount of visits per minute, HTTP requests to ` wp-cron.php` may generate significant overhead by having to negotiate and establish the connection over a network socket. Unauthenticated attackers could abuse this behaviour to achieve denial-of-service (DoS).

WordPress Core contains an XPath injection vulnerability due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input. An attacker could exploit this issue by passing a maliciously crafted string containing XPath syntax and result in the theft of a victim's cookies, session tokens and other sensitive information.

WordPress Core and the WordPress Gutenberg plugin are vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting (XSS). A remote attacker could send a crafted input via a navigation link block to create a page with a stored malicious script, which if viewed by a victim user could result in the theft of their sensitive information or automated actions being performed on their behalf. 

**Note:** This may only be triggered as a "Contributor" role or higher.

Wordpress suffers from an information exposure issue. A remote attacker could read the comments on private and password protected posts, disclosing the sensitive information contained within.

**Note:** The attacker must possess the "Contributor" role or higher to perform this attack.

WordPress contains an information disclosure vulnerability due to insufficient restriction of searchable fields. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this issue to disclose the email addresses of users who have previously published a public post.

WordPress contains an information disclosure vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this to expose internal usernames by sending a POST request and manipulating the REST API to receive this request as if it were a GET request.

Two Cross-Site Scripting vulnerabilities exists in the playlist functionality of WordPress. These issues can be exploited by convincing an Editor or Administrator into uploading a malicious MP3 file. Once uploaded the issues can be triggered by a Contributor or higher using the playlist shortcode.

WordPress Core is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in versions up to, and including,  6.4.3 via the `redirect_guess_404_permalink` function. This can allow unauthenticated attackers to expose the slug of a custom post whose 'publicly_queryable' post status has been set to 'false'.

**Note: CVE details have been utilized in generating this advisory. The details of the vulnerability have not been independently verified by BlackDuck CyRC.**

WordPress Core is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via user display names in the Avatar block in various versions up to 6.5.2 due to insufficient output escaping on the display name. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. In addition, it also makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that have the comment block present and display the comment author's avatar.

**Note: CVE details have been utilized in generating this advisory. The details of the vulnerability have not been independently verified by BlackDuck CyRC.**

WordPress Core is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the HTML API in various versions up to 6.5.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on URLs. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

**Note: CVE details have been utilized in generating this advisory. The details of the vulnerability have not been independently verified by BlackDuck CyRC.**

WordPress Core is vulnerable to authenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting that can be exploited by attackers with access to the WordPress post and page editor, typically consisting of Authors, Contributors, and Editors making it possible to inject arbitrary web scripts into posts and pages that execute if the `the_meta()` function is called on that page.

**Note: CVE details have been utilized in generating this advisory. The details of the vulnerability have not been independently verified by Black Duck CyRC.**

WordPress is vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting (XSS) due to improper neutralization of input during web page generation. This could allow an attacker with Author or higher user privileges to execute malicious scripts, potentially compromising the integrity of the affected web pages.

**Note:** this is low severity vulnerability that requires an attacker to have Author or higher user privileges to execute the attack vector.

In in wp-includes/rest-api/endpoints/class-wp-rest-posts-controller.php in WordPress 3.7 to 5.3.0, authenticated users who do not have the rights to publish a post are able to mark posts as sticky or unsticky via the REST API. For example, the contributor role does not have such rights, but this allowed them to bypass that. This has been patched in WordPress 5.3.1, along with all the previous WordPress versions from 3.7 to 5.3 via a minor release.

In wp-includes/formatting.php in WordPress 3.7 to 5.3.0, the function wp_targeted_link_rel() can be used in a particular way to result in a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This has been patched in WordPress 5.3.1, along with all the previous WordPress versions from 3.7 to 5.3 via a minor release.
Wordpress `Press This` functionality susceptible to CSRF *(Cross-Site Request Forgery)* attacks.
Wordpress fails to  validate user supplied data resulting in XSS *(Cross-Site Scripting attacks)* via Taxonomy Term Name functionality.
Wordpress fails to validate user supplied data resulting in XSS *(Cross-Site Scripting attacks)* when embedding YouTube URL's.

WordPress through 4.8.2, when domain-based flashmediaelement.swf sandboxing is not used, allows remote attackers to conduct cross-domain Flash injection (XSF) attacks by leveraging code contained within the wp-includes/js/mediaelement/flashmediaelement.swf file.

wp-admin/includes/class-wp-press-this.php in Press This in WordPress before 4.7.2 does not properly restrict visibility of a taxonomy-assignment user interface, which allows remote attackers to bypass intended access restrictions by reading terms.
Wordpress administrators my delete unintended files via the `plugin deletion` functionality.

Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in wp-admin/includes/class-wp-posts-list-table.php in the posts list table in WordPress before 4.7.2 allows remote attackers to inject arbitrary web script or HTML via a crafted excerpt.
Wordpress URL redirect validation bypass via control characters.

WordPress users with lower privileges (like contributors) can inject JavaScript code in the block editor using a specific payload, which is executed within the dashboard. This can lead to XSS if an admin opens the post in the editor. Execution of this attack does require an authenticated user. This has been patched in WordPress 5.3.1, along with all the previous WordPress versions from 3.7 to 5.3 via a minor release. Automatic updates are enabled by default for minor releases and we strongly recommend that you keep them enabled.

In WordPress before 5.3.1, authenticated users with lower privileges (like contributors) can inject JavaScript code in the block editor, which is executed within the dashboard. It can lead to an admin opening the affected post in the editor leading to XSS.

A Cross-Site Scripting *(XSS)* vulnerability exists in WordPress prior to **4.7.5** where an attacker could insert malicious code into the name of a large file and trick a user into trying to upload it.  This is due to improper sanitization of the filename, which is included in the error message.

WordPress is vulnerable to an information disclosure issue due to how `pingback.ping` XML-RPC requests can be abused. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted POST requests to the `XMLRPC` endpoint in order to enumerate the titles of private and drafted posts.

**Note:** The vendor does has stated that they will not fix this vulnerability.

WordPress is vulnerable to the insertion of sensitive information into sent data due to improper handling of embedded sensitive data in contributor-level functionalities. This could allow an attacker with contributor-level privileges to retrieve sensitive information embedded in transmitted data.

Wordpress is vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting (XSS). This could allow an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code and obtain sensitive information such as authentication tokens and user session cookies or manipulate how pages are rendered.

WordPress before 4.7.3 has a cross site scripting vulnerability that can be exploited.

This attack can be achieved by tricking an Editor or Administrator into uploading a malicious MP3 file. Once uploaded the issues can be triggered by a Contributor or higher using the playlist shortcode.

Angus Mail and it's predecessors, Jakarta Mail and JavaMail, are vulnerable to an SMTP injection issue due to how `\r` and `\n` UTF-8 characters are mishandled.

In order to exploit this issue, an attacker could submit a crafted Unicode `mail address` value that can be converted into a malicious command when the address is converted to ASCII characters.

Jenkins 2.470 and earlier, LTS 2.452.3 and earlier allows agent processes to read arbitrary files from the Jenkins controller file system by using the `ClassLoaderProxy#fetchJar` method in the Remoting library.

Apache Struts is vulnerable to a path traversal issue due to a flaw present in the file upload logic. `HttpParameters` operations are case-sensitive, meaning it is possible for crafted inputs to bypass checks.

This issue could allow an attacker to manipulate file upload parameters in a manner that permits them to upload malicious files to unintended directories. Executable files could be uploaded to these directories in order to achieve remote code execution (RCE) impacts.

Apache Struts is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE).  This vulnerability only manifests in certain configuration environments.  This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable system with the privileges of the Apache Struts process.  This can lead to a total compromise of a systems confidentiality and integrity, and the possibility to cause a substantial availability impact also.

This vulnerability is listed as exploitable by the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency in their [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

A remote code execution (RCE) attack is possible when using the Struts REST plugin with `XStream` handler to deserialize XML requests.

This vulnerability is listed as exploitable by the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency in their [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

The Struts 1 plug-in provides the ability to use existing Struts 1 Actions and Action forms within Struts 2 applications. Insufficient input validation within the `ActionMessage` class can lead to remote code execution (RCE).

This vulnerability is listed as exploitable by the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency in their [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

Apache Struts2 is vulnerable to RCE through forced double evaluation of powerful OGNL expression statements under certain circumstances. A remote attacker could leverage this to cause remote code execution (RCE) in the context of the web server that hosts a vulnerable Struts2 application.

Apache Struts is susceptible to a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this by passing a maliciously crafted expression, allowing them to execute arbitrary code on the server in the context of the web application.
Apache Struts is prone to remote code execution (RCE) attack when using expressions in FreeMarker tags instead of string literals.

Struts is vulnerable to remote command injection through incorrectly parsing a web client supplied invalid Content-Type, Content-Disposition or Content-Length headers. These commands get executed under the Apache Web user. This is full remote command execution and is being actively exploited in the wild from the initial disclosure.

This vulnerability is listed as exploitable by the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency in their [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

Apache Struts is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) when using the REST plugin and when Dynamic Method Invocation is enabled. An attacker can cause malicious code to be executed on the server side by passing a crafted request  to the application.

Apache Struts 2 is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) through forced OGNL expression statements under certain circumstances. A remote attacker could leverage this to cause RCE in the context of the web server that hosts the vulnerable Struts application.

**Note**: This issue was not properly fixed and required an additional disclosure as **CVE-2021-31805** (**BDSA-2022-1011**).

This vulnerability is listed as exploitable by the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency in their [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

Apache Struts 2 is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) through forced OGNL expression statements under certain circumstances. A remote attacker could leverage this to cause RCE in the context of the web server that hosts the vulnerable Struts application.

**Note:** This vulnerability exists due to an incomplete fix for **CVE-2020-17530** (**BDSA-2020-3670**).
Apache Struts is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) when using the REST plug-in.  An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute system commands on the target machine.

Apache Struts is vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF) through the insufficient validation of session tokens. An authenticated victim must be tricked into visiting a crafted a page in order for the forged request to be sent.

Apache Struts2 is vulnerable to cross-site scripting when using versions of the Java Runtime Environment (JRE) with a broken implementation of `URLDecoder`.  This could allow an attacker to steal tokens, session cookies, credentials or other sensitive information.

Apache Struts2 is vulnerable to code execution via parsing maliciously crafted XSLT files. An attacker able to upload such a file to the server, then view the file from the web server, can cause code execution in the context of the web server user or alter the application state.

**NOTE: BlackDuck CyRC believe that additional versions of Apache Struts are vulnerable . The range of affected versions may be subject to change pending conclusion of Responsible Disclosure.**

A flawed logic issue has been identified in Apache Struts' file upload functionality. An attacker could exploit this by manipulating file upload parameters to enable paths traversal, and under specific circumstances could enable the uploading of malicious files which could be used to perform Remote Code Execution.

**Note:**  Per the Vendor, only applications using `FileUploadInterceptor` are affected.

Apache Struts is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE). This can occur when an attacker forces Struts to evaluate an Object Graph Navigation Library (OGNL) expression twice by supplying a crafted HTML request, resulting in malicious code being executed on the server within the context of the application. This is due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2016-0785 (BDSA-2016-1550).
A remote attacker who can supply specially crafted input to the `TextProvider` interface via actions in Apache Struts can cause remote code execution with the privileges of the web server.

XStream is a Java library to serialize objects to XML and back again. In XStream before version 1.4.15, a Server-Side Forgery Request vulnerability can be activated when unmarshalling. The vulnerability may allow a remote attacker to request data from internal resources that are not publicly available only by manipulating the processed input stream. If you rely on XStream's default blacklist of the Security Framework, you will have to use at least version 1.4.15. The reported vulnerability does not exist if running Java 15 or higher. No user is affected who followed the recommendation to setup XStream's Security Framework with a whitelist! Anyone relying on XStream's default blacklist can immediately switch to a whilelist for the allowed types to avoid the vulnerability. Users of XStream 1.4.14 or below who still want to use XStream default blacklist can use a workaround described in more detailed in the referenced advisories.

Missing XML Validation vulnerability in Apache Struts, Apache Struts.

This issue affects Apache Struts: from 2.0.0 before 2.2.1; Apache Struts: from 2.2.1 through 6.1.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.1.1, which fixes the issue.

Apache Struts is vulnerable to remote code inclusion.  An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by including the URI of a maliciously crafted stylesheet file in a HTTP request to the application, resulting in remote code execution.

Apache Struts is susceptible to a remote code execution vulnerability.  An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying maliciously crafted input via a HTML request, in order to execute arbitrary code on the server in the context of the web application.
Apache Struts contains an improper handling of URLs vulnerability within the Convention plug-in. This can be exploited by crafting special URLs to cause path traversal and arbitrary code execution.

Apache Struts is vulnerable to session tampering and object manipulation due to insufficient restrictions on access to internal objects. This could allow an attacker to modify internal Struts attributes, including session state and container settings.
Apache Struts is vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) due to improper validation of user-supplied input in form fields. An attacker could exploit this issue by crafting a malicious URL.

Apache Struts is vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) due to a file leak during multipart request processing. This could allow a remote attacker to send crafted multipart requests. Successful exploitation could allow for disk exhaustion which could lead to a crash in the application.

**Note**: This vulnerability was assigned a new CVE, **CVE-2025-66675** (**BDSA-2025-54122**), as the original CVE did not specify several vulnerable versions.
Apache Struts is vulnerable to denial-of-service attack via REST plugin when utilizing XStream library to serilaize and deserialize XML objects.
A denial-of-service (DoS) attack is possible when using outdated `XStream` library with the Struts REST plug-in for Apache Struts web framework.
Apache Struts is vulnerable to bypass of access restrictions by a remote attacker who could provide a crafted request and cause the user to be redirected to an invalid location.

If Apache Struts takes an URL in a form field and the built-in `URLValidator` functionality is utilized, an attacker can craft special input which will overload the server process. This leads to a denial-of-service (DoS).

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache Software Foundation Apache Struts.This issue affects Apache Struts: through 2.5.30, through 6.1.2.

Upgrade to Struts 2.5.31 or 6.1.2.1 or greater.

Apache Struts is vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS) due to insufficient input sanitization in the functionality intended for displaying the language selected by the user. A malicious user can inject arbitrary web script payload into the parameter intended for changing the language which will be triggered if a developer tries to list the language selected by the user. This flaw can be leveraged to steal a victim's session cookies.
An improper input validation vulnerability has been discovered in Apache Struts. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by a crafted input to perform unspecified attacks against the system.

XStream is a Java library to serialize objects to XML and back again. In XStream before version 1.4.15, is vulnerable to an Arbitrary File Deletion on the local host when unmarshalling. The vulnerability may allow a remote attacker to delete arbitrary know files on the host as log as the executing process has sufficient rights only by manipulating the processed input stream. If you rely on XStream's default blacklist of the Security Framework, you will have to use at least version 1.4.15. The reported vulnerability does not exist running Java 15 or higher. No user is affected, who followed the recommendation to setup XStream's Security Framework with a whitelist! Anyone relying on XStream's default blacklist can immediately switch to a whilelist for the allowed types to avoid the vulnerability. Users of XStream 1.4.14 or below who still want to use XStream default blacklist can use a workaround described in more detailed in the referenced advisories.

Apache Struts contains a denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to send crafted multipart requests containing files to upload, that will fail a validation check, but consequently still upload the files to the Struts Multipart save file directory location. This can be used to consume disk space on the server, degrading the service or potentially causing a crash.

Apache Struts contains an information disclosure vulnerability due to improper use of the Config Browser plugin within a production environment. An attacker could exploit this to expose application information.

Apache Struts contains a denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability. An attacker is able to enter a null value for a URL field within the `URLValidator` class due to an overly permissive regular expression. This can lead to a crash.
A denial-of-service (DoS) attack is possible against Apache Struts2 when using the `URLValidator` class to validate an `URL` provided in a form field.

Apache Struts is vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) due to a file leak during multipart request processing. This could allow a remote attacker to send crafted multipart requests. Successful exploitation could allow for disk exhaustion which could lead to a crash in the application.

**Note**: This vulnerability was originally assigned **BDSA-2025-40342** (**CVE-2025-64775**), however it was assigned a new CVE as the original CVE did not mention several versions which were vulnerable.

Apache Struts 2.0.0 through 2.3.24.1 does not properly cache method references when used with OGNL before 3.0.12, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (block access to a web site) via unspecified vectors.
Apache Struts is vulnerable to open redirect due to input validation bypass on the return string. An attacker is able to craft a malicious URL to redirect a user to an unvalidated location.

Apache Struts contains an out-of-memory condition vulnerability due to insufficient validation of the sizes of non-file normal form fields in multipart requests. A privileged attacker could exploit this issue by passing a multipart request to a vulnerable instance which could trigger a denial-of-service (DoS) condition via excessive resource allocation.

Apache Struts2 contains a denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability.  This vulnerability requires an attacker to have the ability to upload a file to the server.  Under certain conditions, a remote attacker can then change the permissions of files and directories to read only.  This will prevent certain actions from working, causing errors.  This can be used to cause a denial-of-service.
An authenticated attacker can cause a denial of service when the application uses Spring AOP functionality to secure Struts action.

The Struts 1 ActionForm object allowed access to the `class` parameter, which is directly mapped to the `getClass()` method. A remote attacker could use this flaw to manipulate the `ClassLoader` used by an application server running Struts 1. This could lead to remote code execution under certain conditions, allowing unauthorised disclosure of information, unauthorised modification and disruption of service.

Apache Commons BeanUtils is distributed in `lib/commons-beanutils-1.8.0.jar` in Apache Struts **1.x** to **1.3.10** and in other products requiring commons-beanutils (to version **1.9.2**)

Apache Commons BeanUtils introduced a fix for BDSA-2014-0001 (CVE-2014-0114), however did not enable the protections by default. A remote attacker could leverage this to cause code execution in applications that did not use the new security feature.

Apache Commons BeanUtils introduced a feature to protect against access to the classloader through various mechanisms. The `declaredClass` property of Java enum objects is a vector for classloader access and not protected against by default. If an application passes property paths from an attacker directly to the `getProperty()` method of `PropertyUtilsBean`, the attacker can access the enumâs class loader via the `declaredClass` property. This can result in remote code execution (RCE).

A sandbox bypass vulnerability exists in Jenkins Matrix Project Plugin 1.13 and earlier in pom.xml, src/main/java/hudson/matrix/FilterScript.java that allows attackers with Job/Configure permission to execute arbitrary code on the Jenkins master JVM.

Jenkins Matrix Project Plugin 1.16 and earlier does not escape the node names shown in tooltips on the overview page of builds with a single axis, resulting in a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability.

Jenkins Matrix Project Plugin 1.16 and earlier does not escape the axis names shown in tooltips on the overview page of builds with multiple axes, resulting in a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability.

Jenkins Matrix Project Plugin 1.19 and earlier does not escape HTML metacharacters in node and label names, and label descriptions, resulting in a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exploitable by attackers with Agent/Configure permission.

Jenkins Matrix Project Plugin 822.v01b_8c85d16d2 and earlier does not sanitize user-defined axis names of multi-configuration projects, allowing attackers with Item/Configure permission to create or replace any config.xml files on the Jenkins controller file system with content not controllable by the attackers.

Apache ant is vulnerable to an arbitrary file write vulnerability via a directory traversal. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying the component with a maliciously crafted archive that, when unpacked, would cause an arbitrary file to be written to the file system.
Apache Ant is vulnerable to information disclosure due to the usage of a default temporary directory for several tasks. Some tasks may also allow the integrity of a build to be damaged.
Apache Ant is vulnerable to information disclosure due to the usage of a default temporary directory for several tasks. Some tasks may also allow the integrity of a build to be damaged.

Apache Ant is vulnerable to an out of memory error via a crafted `TAR` archive. An attacker could exploit this in order to cause as denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

**Note:** Per the Vendor, "Versions prior to 1.9.0 are not affected when reading tar archives.".
Apache Ant is vulnerable to an out of memory error via a crafted `ZIP` archive. An attacker could exploit this in order to cause as denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

Apache Commons contains a flaw that is due to the Base32 codec decoding  invalid strings instead of rejecting them. This may allow a remote attacker to tunnel  additional information via a base 32 string that seems valid.

Express.js web framework is vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) due to the improper handling of user input in the `response.redirect()` function. This could allow an attacker to execute JavaScript code on the users browser.

**Note** The attacker must be in control of the input to `response.redirect()` and the user must click before the redirect occurs.

qs before 6.10.3, as used in Express before 4.17.3 and other products, allows attackers to cause a Node process hang for an Express application because an __ proto__ key can be used. In many typical Express use cases, an unauthenticated remote attacker can place the attack payload in the query string of the URL that is used to visit the application, such as a[__proto__]=b&a[__proto__]&a[length]=100000000. The fix was backported to qs 6.9.7, 6.8.3, 6.7.3, 6.6.1, 6.5.3, 6.4.1, 6.3.3, and 6.2.4 (and therefore Express 4.17.3, which has "deps: qs@6.9.7" in its release description, is not vulnerable).

Express.js contains an open redirect vulnerability due to insufficient validation of user supplied URLs. An attacker could exploit this by providing a crafted URL when performing a redirect bypassing the redirect allow list leading to an open redirect.
Xstream is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) by an attacker who can supply a specially crafted input stream.

XStream is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) due to the unsafe deserialization of classes. A remote attacker could execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable server by causing that server to deserialize a maliciously crafted serialized object.

XStream is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) due to the unsafe deserialization of classes. A remote attacker could execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable server by causing that server to deserialize a maliciously crafted serialized object.

Xstream is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) through specially crafted input. A remote attacker is able to execute arbitrary system commands on the host machine if Xstream's security framework has been configured with a default blacklist, rather than the more secure whitelisting method.

XStream is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) due to the unsafe deserialization of classes. A remote attacker could execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable server by causing that server to deserialize a maliciously crafted serialized object.

XStream is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) due to the unsafe deserialization of classes. A remote attacker could execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable server by causing that server to deserialize a maliciously crafted serialized object.

XStream is vulnerable to unsafe deserialization of user-controlled input. A remote attacker could leverage this to execute arbitrary code from a remote server.

**Note:** If the application uses XStream's security framework and whitelist approach to deserialization (recommended), it is not vulnerable.

XStream is vulnerable to unsafe deserialization of attacker controlled input. A remote attacker could leverage this to execute arbitrary code from a remote server.

**Note** If the application uses XStreams security framework and whitelist approach to deserialization (recommended), it is not vulnerable.

XStream is vulnerable to unsafe deserialization of attacker controlled input. A remote attacker could leverage this to execute arbitrary system commands.

Note that if the application uses XStream's security framework and allowlist approach to deserialization (recommended), it is not vulnerable.

This vulnerability is listed as exploitable by the Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency in their [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog).

XStream is vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) due to the unsafe demarshalling of CORBA and XSLTC classes. A remote attacker could execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable server by causing that server to deserialize a maliciously crafted serialized object.

XStream, when in its default configuration or operating without a sufficient blacklist / whitelist configuration, is vulnerable to an arbitrary code execution issue. This is due to how XStream can potentially create new instances of dangerous objects that are not blocked based on the contents of the input stream. The potentially dangerous type in this case are `javafx.collections.ObservableList` and `JavacProcessingEnvironment$NameProcessIterator`.

An attacker could supply a crafted input to XStream in order execute arbitrary code stored on a remote host.

XStream is vulnerable to server-side request forgery (SSRF) by a remote attacker who can supply a specially crafted input stream to modify or inject objects. This allows them to request data from the internal network that the XStream application is hosted on.

Those using Woodstox to parse XML data may be vulnerable to Denial of Service attacks (DOS) if DTD support is enabled. If the parser is running on user supplied input, an attacker may supply content that causes the parser to crash by stackoverflow. This effect may support a denial of service attack.

XStream, when using some supported parsers, is vulnerable to an XML entity expansion issue due to how these parsers can process external entities by default.

A remote attacker could use this issue to retrieve the content of arbitrary files with known locations in a local file system if the Java process has read access.

**Note**: XStream is not vulnerable if the default XML Pull Parser (`Xpp3` or `kXML2`) is used. These parser types do not process XML entities.

XStream, when in its default configuration or operating without a sufficient blacklist / whitelist configuration, is vulnerable to a server-side request forgery (SSRF) issue. This is due to how XStream can potentially create new instances of dangerous objects that are not blocked based on the contents of the input stream. The potentially dangerous types in this case are `sun.awt.datatransfer.DataTransferer$IndexOrderComparator` and `javax.activation.URLDataSource`.

An attacker could supply a crafted input to XStream in order request information from internal resources.

XStream is vulnerable to an arbitrary file deletion flaw in it's handling of unmarshalling specially crafted input. A remote attacker could delete arbitrary files on the server, if the server process has sufficient rights. As well as impacting the integrity of data, this might lead to a denial-of-service (DoS) of applications on the system that rely on specific files for their operation.

XStream, when in its default configuration or operating without a sufficient blacklist / whitelist configuration, is vulnerable to an arbitrary code execution issue. This is due to how XStream can potentially create new instances of dangerous objects that are not blocked based on the contents of the input stream.
